title: Wikipedia car example - complete hierarchy with alternatives
description: The Jones family car-buying example that serves as Wikipedia's standing worked illustration of AHP, as a complete three-level hierarchy: four criteria, six subcriteria under Cost and Capacity, and six Honda models compared under all eight covering criteria (11 judgment matrices, 133 pairwise comparisons). The criteria and subcriteria judgments are stated in the article's prose; the alternative-level judgments are published in the article's judgment-table images and were transcribed from them (each matrix cites its image). Transcription was verified three ways: entry-by-entry against the images; by reproducing the article's own displayed local priorities at their printed precision under the column-normalization approximation; and against the interactive decision linked from the article's External links section, which contains identical judgments. Expected values are derived with the principal-eigenvector method, with column-normalization alternates for every inconsistent matrix; all values the article itself displays are preserved in source_reported, where their relationship to both methods is explained.

source.notes: Criteria judgments are in the article's prose; Cost and Capacity subcriteria judgments are in a footnote ('Purchase Price 2 over Fuel Cost, 5 over Maintenance Cost, and 3 over Resale Value; Fuel Cost 2 over Maintenance Cost and 2 over Resale Value; Maintenance Cost -2 vs. Resale Value'; 'Cargo Capacity -5 vs. Passenger Capacity' - negative values meaning the left element is less important). Alternative judgments are in the article's judgment-table images (named per matrix). Fuel Costs judgments are the article's MPG ratios to two decimals (e.g. 1.13 = 35/31 MPG); Purchase Price, Maintenance and Resale judgments include the non-integer intensities 1.5 and 1.2 exactly as the images show. An interactive version containing these judgments is linked from the article's External links: https://app.decisionpoint.io/ahp/processes/1u7fb2loziitknizzy7baon5t

scale.name: saaty-1-9
scale.notes: Judgments on Saaty's fundamental 1-9 scale; reciprocals and fractional/decimal values are valid entries (the article's Fuel Costs judgments are decimal MPG ratios). Matrix entries may be numbers or fraction strings such as "1/3" or "1/1.13".

source_reported.explanation: All numeric results the article displays are consistent with the column-normalization approximation: the alternate expected values in this fixture reproduce the article's local priorities at their printed three decimals, its global priorities within 0.002, and its final priorities (from the AHPJonesFinalPriorities.png synthesis table) within 0.002. The exact principal-eigenvector results differ from the displayed values by up to about 0.003 at the factor level and 0.003 at the final level, without changing the ranking (Odyssey first, Accord Sedan second, then CR-V, Accord Hybrid, Element, Pilot). The article does not state which prioritization method its software used. Neither set of values is wrong; they are the outputs of different documented methods applied to the same judgments.
source_reported.citation: 'Analytic hierarchy process - car example', Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analytic_hierarchy_process_%E2%80%93_car_example (accessed 2026-11-16). Criteria and global priorities from the article's text and synthesis table; local priorities from the article's per-criterion tables; final priorities from the AHPJonesFinalPriorities.png image.
